recompute.my_rule: knee axis: right RKNE-RMKNE, left LMKNE-LKNE (points to the person's right), horizontal part; leg-plane forward = up x axis; thigh and shank = Transforms_Euler y axes (YZX file order) measured in that plane from straight down; foot = heel to mean(MT1,MT5) measured from the plane forward; pelvis = elevation of mid-ASIS minus mid-PSIS above its horizontal part (own plane); joints as differences; speeds wrapped central difference at 200 Hz; planar CoP: frame axes anterior = cos t f + sin t up, vertical = -sin t f + cos t up (t = foot angle), lateral = plane normal outward, origin = ankle midpoint + 0.1 m along anterior, plate point (COPX, COPY_Vertical, COPZ) loaded at 20 N or more

planar_cop_judgement.what_the_worker_did: anterior axis = heel-to-toe projected into the leg plane; origin 100 mm along that planar axis from the ankle midpoint; lateral = plane normal outward; the 3-D heel-to-toe frame is retired
planar_cop_judgement.match_with_standard: Does not fully match. The standard (index.md, CoP frame, 23 Nov 2026) puts the origin 100 mm forward of the ankle centre along the foot's heel-to-toe direction, forward along the foot, up perpendicular to it, sideways outward. With toe-out the planar axis is not the heel-to-toe line, so the origin leaves the foot's own line, and the toe-out appears as a sideways shift of the whole frame. It is consistent only when the foot's heel-to-toe line lies in the leg plane. The new side-view-plane line ('CoP and foot frame follow the new foot plane') is ambiguous and can be read as the worker did.
planar_cop_judgement.evidence: Toe-out (heel-to-toe horizontal direction against the leg-plane forward) has median absolute values of 2 to 22 degrees by recording and leg (e.g. AB10 meander right 22, AB09 stairs left 20, AB13 normal_walk left 15), p95 higher. Distance between the planar origin and the 3-D heel-to-toe origin: median 0.4 to 3.6 cm, 95th percentile about 5 to 8 cm, maximum 9.4 cm (AB11 turn_and_step_1 right 9.5 cm, AB10 right 9.4 cm). Against the retired 3-D frame the planar CoP lateral coordinate moves outward by a median 1 to 2 cm (AB13 normal_walk left 0.5 to 2.5 cm median, right 0.0 to 1.1; AB05 left 0.3 to 1.8; AB10 meander left 0.3 to 2.4; AB03 right unchanged), while the anterior coordinate changes by only 0.0 to 0.5 cm. In the 3-D frame the lateral median was about 0.0 to 0.8 cm, i.e. the pressure point ran along the foot line; in the planar frame it carries the toe-out offset.
planar_cop_judgement.flag: Flag for José / the standard owner: either amend the standard to say the CoP frame is planar (origin and axes in the leg plane), or keep the origin on the foot's own heel-to-toe line and use the plane only for the angles. Not changed here. Steps 2-4 inherit whichever is chosen.

l5_rise.question: Why L5 went from 90 to 108 failing observations, with AB03 holding 70.
l5_rise.answer: Not the leg-plane frame mishandling AB03's geometry, and not a missing-ASIS effect. Two separate things. (a) The rise is mostly observations that sit just past the limit: 85 of the 90 earlier L5 observations still fail, 23 are new and 5 dropped; the new ones exceed their limit by a median of 1.3 cm (17 of 23 within 2 cm, largest 10.4 cm in one AB02 cutting_1 time table), the dropped ones by 0.5 cm or less. The plane frame moves anterior and vertical coordinates by a few centimetres, enough to push marginal samples either way. (b) The AB03 failures themselves (61 earlier, 70 now; 58 in both) are real bad pressure points that fail in every frame.
l5_rise.ab03_asis: The ASIS markers are present in the AB03 recordings I read (side_shuffle_1, incline_walk_2, normal_walk_1 all have LASI and RASI). The step-1 ledger holds LASI-dependent columns only in AB03 walk_backward_1 and weighted_walk_1. The leg plane and the pressure-point frame use knee, ankle, heel and toe markers, not ASIS, so ASIS cannot move the pressure point.

evidence.AB03_side_shuffle_1 (15 of the 70 observ: left foot: 920 failing loaded samples, lateral -0.645 to -0.530 m (limit 0.3), median toe-out 9 degrees (0.9 to 20), plate pressure point 0.53 to 0.65 m horizontally from the ankle and 0.53 to 0.65 m from the marker foot line, median force 869 N (0.78 BW). Right foot: 1,287 samples, lateral -0.669 to -0.301 m, toe-out median 4 degrees (-18 to 13), 0.27 to 0.69 m from the marker foot, median force 539 N (0.48 BW). In the retired 3-D heel-to-toe frame 920 of 920 (left) and 1,267 of 1,287 (right) fail the same way, lateral within about 1 cm of the plane value. Passing loaded samples of the same recording sit 0.05 m from the marker foot (95th percentile 0.056 to 0.069), so the plate pressure point is about 0.5 m away from the foot at high load: a plate/marker mismatch (unlabelled source geometry), not toe-out.
evidence.AB03_incline_walk_2 (42 observations; ve: left foot 70 failing loaded samples (vertical 58, anterior 12) at median force 62 N (0.06 BW, 53 to 79 N, just above the 20 N loading cut), pressure point 0.25 to 0.54 m from the ankle and 0.27 to 0.48 m from the marker foot; right foot 41 samples (vertical 38, lateral 3) at median 63 N, 0.35 to 0.63 m away. Toe-out at failing left samples is large (median 38 degrees, 7 to 46) but lateral values there are only 0.04 to 0.22 m and none fails on lateral, and 0 of 70 (left) and 3 of 41 (right) fail in the old 3-D frame lateral test, so the failures are vertical/anterior, near-unloaded samples (heel contact or toe-off at 0.06 BW) where the plate pressure point is noisy.
evidence.AB03_normal_walk_1 (12 observations): 3 left and 8 right failing samples, force 48 to 70 N (about 0.05 BW), 0.32 to 0.62 m from the ankle; same low-load pattern. AB13 normal_walk_1 shows the same effect at 1 sample (51 N, toe-out 25 degrees, lateral -0.24 m, within limits).
evidence.toe_out: Passing loaded samples have toe-out of 2 to 19 degrees (absolute median) and pressure points 0.044 to 0.057 m from the marker foot, so toe-out up to about 25 to 30 degrees does not cause failure. The plane and old frames differ by about 1 cm in lateral.

l5_rise.conclusion: The 108 is the same population of real bad pressure points as before (AB03 side_shuffle_1 plate misfit; near-unloaded samples in incline and normal walking) plus a net 18 marginal observations at the limit edge. The leg-plane frame does not introduce the AB03 failures. L5 limits stay draft; no tuning suggested by this check.

tests.memory_error_cause: tests/test_gt23_raw_kinematics.py::test_actual_receipt_shapes_prepare_and_persisted_run (time and phase) calls audit_gt23_raw_kinematics.run(), whose line 220 does resource.setrlimit(RLIMIT_AS, 768 MiB) and os.nice in the pytest process itself. The limit is never restored, so every test that runs after it in a wide 'pytest -k gt23' (pyarrow, numpy allocations) is capped at 768 MiB of address space and can print a MemoryError. Run alone, the file passes and no test prints a MemoryError. Pre-existing (last changed 98b2364), unrelated to PL01. The exact victim test in the wide run was not reproduced: a wide run was refused by the permission classifier.
tests.suggested_fix: restore the old limit in a fixture (monkeypatch resource.setrlimit or run the test in a subprocess); not changed here.
